cap.line: repo_model.s3c_candidate.cap_line on the target day of each cell: the Standing Repo Facility minimum bid less IORB (repo_model.srf_line.srf_line_bps) from metadata/policy_events.json, read from the entries announced at or before the decision instant and effective by the target; None (no cap) unless the entry in force states no aggregate operation limit (full allotment). The line a baseline is capped at is exactly the candidate's, cell for cell: the study refuses to write a record if a baseline's line differs from the candidate's on any cell
cap.rule: q'_p = min(q_p, line) for every level p on a cell with a line; the cell is unchanged otherwise. Monotone, fits nothing, tunes nothing
cap.probabilities: P(> tau) of every model, capped or not, is capped_law.exceedance(uncapped quantiles, line, tau, rule 'open_tail'): rule (b), as the candidate reads it. Where a cell has no line, or the model is uncapped, no cap is applied and the law is the status-quo law of the quantile vector (what rule (b) gives with no cap). Whole basis points, the event strict (data.exceeds_bp)
cap.information_set: the availability declaration of metadata/srf_cap_1241.json holds unchanged; the instant is the 18:00 decision instant, and tests/test_capped_baselines_1421.py perturbs a policy entry announced after it

windows.development: decision days whose five targets fall on or before 2025-12-31 (window 'development' of scripts/s3c_announced_settlement_1288.py). It is the window that decides what this study reads; the cells at full allotment in it are the targets from 2025-12-11
windows.2026: decision days whose five targets fall from 2026-01-02 to 2026-09-03 (window '2026', the near-blind tier open since GO #151), where full allotment applies on every target; shown apart. The days have been seen by earlier studies

measures.scores: per cell (decision day, lead 1 to 5) and per model: grid CRPS (23 levels; primary, averaged over h = 1..5), upper-tail twCRPS (key secondary) and the Brier score of P(> +5 bp). The grid CRPS and the twCRPS read the model's quantile vector, which is the capped vector for a capped model
measures.groups: pooled (all cells); the cells at full allotment (target days with a line); by regime and by pressure-day type of the target day (turn_days.reporting_day_type). A pooled figure alone is not a result
measures.comparisons: paired, studentized stationary bootstrap (scoring protocol v1), read on the bound on mean d (her ruling on #1009), seed 1421 (kept from #1421 so that the candidate, B1'* and B1'*-cap rows reproduce #1422's page), mean block sp.BLOCK_LENGTH, two-sided 90% interval, on decision-day means over the group's cells: (1) the candidate against each of the four baselines (B1'*, B1'*-cap, B2*, B2*-cap) (positive favours the candidate); (2) each capped baseline against its uncapped version (positive favours the cap: the part of a gain the cap alone buys). A group of fewer than 20 decision days is not tested; a group the two score alike on every day is `identical`. The reading is `gain` when the interval excludes zero on the positive side, `loss` when on the negative side, `undecided` otherwise
measures.share_explained: for each baseline and each metric in the pooled and full-allotment groups: share = (mean uncapped baseline - mean capped baseline) / (mean uncapped baseline - mean candidate), the part of the candidate's gain over the uncapped baseline that the cap alone buys. It is reported only where the candidate's gain over the uncapped baseline is positive and its interval (comparison 1) excludes zero; otherwise it is `not defined`. Its interval is the 90% percentile interval of the share over the stationary bootstrap resamples of the decision days (block as above, seed 1421, 2000 resamples), taken only on resamples whose candidate gain is positive, with the number dropped listed. A share above 1 means the cap alone gains more than the candidate does over the uncapped baseline
measures.reproduction: the pooled mean grid CRPS of the candidate equals the 1314 record, that of the uncapped B1'* the 1388 result, that of B2* the 1420 result (docs/research/b2-star-1420/result.json, B2_star), and the candidate, B1'* and B1'*-cap equal #1422's result (docs/research/capped-baselines-1421/result.json), all to 1e-9 in both windows, or no record is written. Plain B2 and the stand-in B2-cap are copied from #1422's result beside B2*-cap, labelled as the stand-in

reading_rules: Development data, not a verdict. The development window decides what this page reads; the 2026 days are shown apart and have been seen.

A gain or loss is read from the interval on mean d excluding zero; a point estimate alone is not read. A pooled figure is never read without the full-allotment, regime and pressure-day-type groups beside it.
The capped baselines are the confirmatory benchmarks (her ruling of 3 November 2026); the uncapped versions are reported beside them. This study does not reopen that.
Lens C's caveat is stated on the page: the lag-10 HAC standard error is understated about 2x after 2020, so an interval that excludes zero is narrower than it should be.

B2*-cap is the confirmatory benchmark with B2* in it (her ruling of 3 November 2026 on #1421, applied by 4 November's on #1434). The page states plainly what it shows against B2*-cap on the 2026 days' upper-tail twCRPS and Brier score, where the uncapped B2* already had lower means than the candidate in #1420.
Nothing is adopted: not B2*, not B2*-cap, not any change to the confirmation design or to #1394. The candidate stays frozen.
questions: None for her: which version is confirmatory is ruled, and the B2* stand-in is replaced as she ordered. What the page shows against B2*-cap bears on #1394's revision and is hers to weigh.
long_run: one walk of (s3c-ann-net) per window, minutes each, and the paired tests a minute or two each: a cloud run, under the two-hour line of `long-run`
